source.title: CrossQ: Batch Normalization in Deep Reinforcement Learning for Greater Sample Efficiency and Simplicity
source.authors: Aditya Bhatt; Daniel Palenicek; B. Belousov; Max J. Argus; Artemij Amiranashvili; T. Brox; Jan Peters

record.tranche_reason: Tests BatchNorm's effect on learning in off-policy deep reinforcement learning, a new setting for the training-speed claim in V6.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own BatchNorm ablations and learning outcomes. Results cited from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures reinforcement-learning episodic returns per environment interaction, rather than V6's accuracy gains during network training. Sample efficiency can change through policy, data-distribution, and algorithm changes without showing faster optimization of a fixed training objective. No training-accuracy, critic-loss convergence, or learning-rate-tolerance comparison tests the stated versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they attribute CrossQ's sample-efficiency gains chiefly to combining target-network removal with carefully applied BatchNorm, with wider critics adding gains. They report improved long-term stability with BRN. Their assertion that this reproduces supervised learning's training acceleration is an interpretation; the reported measurements are episodic returns rather than training accuracy or fixed-objective optimization speed.
record.recipe_differences: Applies BatchNorm/BRN in off-policy reinforcement learning and measures episodic-return sample efficiency, rather than supervised classification accuracy or training classification error. The CrossQ recipe also removes target networks and changes other algorithm components.
record.method_sensitivity: The BatchNorm effect depends on retaining versus removing target networks; original BN versus BRN; normalization in the critic only versus actor and critic; and BatchNorm versus LayerNorm.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing target networks alone modestly improves SAC sample efficiency; adding BN after removal gives the strongest aggregate improvement, whereas BN with target networks fails to learn in half the environments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization can improve off-policy actor-critic sample efficiency when target networks are removed and current and next-state batches share normalization statistics.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing BRN causes CrossQ training to diverge; replacing it with LayerNorm produces slower learning and returns roughly at SAC's level.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CrossQ's RL performance depends on its normalization method.

fits_no_version.finding: Original BN sometimes suffers later return collapses; BRN with momentum 0.99 or higher avoids these in the reported runs. Critic-only BRN retains strong performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization variant, moving-average momentum, and placement affect CrossQ's long-term learning stability.

record.problems: Evidence concerns continuous-control episodic returns rather than classification accuracy or training error. Several ablation conclusions are qualitative summaries of plots; the text does not give exact values for those comparisons. The target-network and BatchNorm ablation uses tanh activations to avoid divergence and uses original BN, whereas CrossQ uses BRN.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results omitted. Cited results from other studies and CrossQ-versus-baseline comparisons that do not isolate a claim component were not extracted.

untested.parts: All: convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random or corrupted labels.
All: teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.
All: depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
All: initialization-dependent learning speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
All: learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss recovery, and curvature dynamics.
All stated components: faster accuracy gains with BatchNorm, higher learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons. The RL-return ablations address a related claim.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text is sufficient for this assessment. No exact return values or environment-specific failure identities can be recovered reliably from its flattened plots. The related RL findings do not justify verdicts on the stated claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and spurious local minima.
Depth-related training error in plain versus residual networks; deep tanh and Fixup results are cited background.
Initialization comparisons and training depth in plain networks.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, curvature, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Does not test sigmoid networks on MNIST, VGG on CIFAR-10, Inception on ImageNet, learning-rate tolerance, or Fixup residual networks.

rows.subject: SAC (tanh)
rows.operation_detail: Trained without target networks, using tanh critic activations and no BatchNorm.

conditions.value: six continuous-control environments: Humanoid, Ant, HumanoidStandup, HalfCheetah, Walker2d, Hopper

rows.measure: IQM episodic return over environment steps (sample efficiency)
rows.value: Removing target networks (-TN) provides only small improvements over the SAC baseline with target nets.
rows.note: This is the no-BatchNorm comparator for the BatchNorm ablation; the result is stated qualitatively.
rows.check: Measures target-network removal without BatchNorm; it is a control for the RL experiment, not evidence of V6's effect.

rows.subject: SAC (tanh + BN)
rows.operation_detail: Added original BatchNorm to the critic while retaining target networks.

conditions.value: six continuous-control environments: Humanoid, Ant, HumanoidStandup, HalfCheetah, Walker2d, Hopper

rows.measure: IQM episodic return over environment steps (sample efficiency)
rows.value: BatchNorm with target nets is unstable, failing to learn anything in half of the environments.
rows.note: The text reports failures in half the environments; it does not name which environments in this sentence.
rows.check: Failure to learn in half the environments concerns episodic returns, not the training-accuracy or learning-rate effect named in V6.

rows.subject: SAC (tanh + BN)
rows.operation_detail: Added original BatchNorm to the critic and removed target networks.

conditions.value: six continuous-control environments: Humanoid, Ant, HumanoidStandup, HalfCheetah, Walker2d, Hopper

rows.measure: IQM episodic return over environment steps (sample efficiency)
rows.baseline: SAC variants with tanh activations; the paper says this configuration achieves the best aggregate performance
rows.value: BatchNorm without target networks achieves the best aggregate performance; the boost is significantly bigger than from removing target networks alone.
rows.note: The authors describe this as the configuration closest to CrossQ.
rows.check: The reported improvement is RL sample efficiency under target-network removal and joint-batch normalization, not training accuracy.

rows.subject: CrossQ (ours)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Batch Renormalization (BRN) in actor and critic, using the CrossQ recipe.
rows.value: CrossQ ablations show removing BRN gives the worst overall performance; the paper says CrossQ's BRN configuration improves learning.
rows.uncertainty: 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals for Figure 9; six seeds per environment
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative summary of the aggregate ablation rather than exact plotted values.
rows.check: This is a CrossQ component ablation measured by episodic returns. Figure 9 reports percentage loss in IQM return relative to full CrossQ; the relevant comparator is CrossQ without BRN, not SAC.

rows.subject: CrossQ (ours)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with original BatchNorm instead of BRN.

conditions.value: four plotted environments: Humanoid, HumanoidStandup, Ant, Hopper

rows.measure: IQM episodic return over environment steps (sample efficiency)
rows.value: Original BatchNorm is prone to sudden performance collapses during longer training runs.
rows.note: The text says early sample efficiency is similar across variants and describes later collapses for BN.
rows.check: Compares BN with BRN using policy returns and later performance collapses; it does not compare accuracy gains with versus without normalization.

rows.subject: CrossQ (ours)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with BRN in the critic only, omitting normalization from the actor.

conditions.value: four plotted environments: Humanoid, HumanoidStandup, Ant, Hopper

rows.measure: IQM episodic return over environment steps (sample efficiency)
rows.baseline: CrossQ with BRN in actor and critic
rows.value: Omitting normalization in the actor does not significantly affect CrossQ; using BatchNorm only in the critic is sufficient for strong performance, while both networks perform slightly better.
rows.note: The authors describe a small performance difference between critic-only and actor-plus-critic normalization.
rows.check: Compares placement of BRN using episodic returns. The negligible actor-normalization benefit does not establish a partial V6 effect.

rows.subject: CrossQ (ours)
rows.measure: IQM episodic return over environment steps (sample efficiency)
rows.value: Replacing BatchNorm with LayerNorm degrades CrossQ's performance significantly, roughly to the SAC baseline level.
rows.note: This compares normalization choices; the paper does not provide exact values in the text.
rows.check: Compares normalization methods through RL returns. Figure 9's baseline is full CrossQ using BRN, and its aggregate measure is percentage loss in IQM return.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
